title: Source layers
summary: A fixed copy of the UN Geodata 2023 polygons and lines, the GAUL 2025 polygons and cells, and reference cells for islands, with every code in upper case as ISO 3166-1 user-assigned codes are, plus the land GAUL and UN Geodata polygons give to different entities.
why: Everything after this point can be traced back to these files.

title: Split into parts
summary: Each UN Geodata row is separated into its individual polygons, so every island and mainland can be handled alone.
why: An island can belong to a different GAUL entity than the mainland of the same UN row.

title: Cut the mainlands
summary: Mainland parts are cut where GAUL has an entity that UN Geodata 2023 draws inside a neighbour. UN lines are used where they exist. GAUL lines are used for the India-China areas, where UN has none.
why: Each disputed area becomes a separate piece, so keeping or dissolving it stays an open choice.

title: Attribute to GAUL
summary: Every piece is given a GAUL entity as a whole, so an island is never divided. A piece takes the GAUL entity its UN entity links to in gaul_links, unless island_overrides gives it to another entity for a listed change. Parts of codes FieldMaps splits into several units are tagged with the unit whose cell holds them.
why: GAUL keeps all of its entities but follows UN Geodata's ownership, so a piece moves only through a listed change, such as the islands off the Hala'ib coast.

title: Units and crosswalk
summary: Pieces with the same UN entity, GAUL entity, area and FieldMaps unit are grouped into units. Each unit gets its output row: its ISO code, numbered ISO3_1, ISO3_2 and so on, largest first, where a code has several rows. The crosswalk links each unit to both sources, and every change is listed.
why: The units are the build layer, and the crosswalk links each unit to its UN and GAUL entity.

title: Dissolve and check
summary: The units are dissolved by UN key for the page and by output row for the ADM0 output, then compared with the sources.
why: The units still add up to every UN Geodata 2023 row, every GAUL entity is kept and each output row has its own id.

title: Extend into water
summary: The units grow outward into the surrounding water to form cells that cover the whole map.
why: Cells keep the political divisions separate from the coastline, so stage 08 can apply OSM's coastline without deciding ownership again.

title: OSM coastline
summary: OSM land replaces UN Geodata's coastline. An OSM polygon with land of one unit goes to that unit whole, and one with land of several units is cut by their cells. One with no UN Geodata land goes to the entity whose waters hold it, and disputed islands become entities of their own. UN Geodata land with no OSM land is dropped.
why: OSM's coastline is more detailed and recent, and every island UN Geodata lacks gets an owner without changing the owner of any land UN Geodata has.

title: Names and attributes
summary: Each output row takes its UN M49 name, its UN Geodata status and FieldMaps' map label. Split rows and user-assigned codes take FieldMaps' names, and name_overrides corrects any field of a row.
why: The output's names and attributes come from the UN reference.

title: Map tiles
summary: Map tiles for the build page, cut from the layers of the earlier stages.
why: The page draws exactly what the stages produced.

title: Page text and tables
summary: The change list with each change's title, description and sources, the page's steps and the tables the page loads.
why: All the text comes from the curated files and the change data in one place, so a text edit reruns only this stage.
